jurisdiction.name: Belize
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Belize has no AI-specific law or AI strategy. Its National Digital Agenda 2026-2030, endorsed by Cabinet in May 2026, commits the government to adopt AI in a targeted and ethical way that safeguards human rights, equity, privacy and transparency, and notes that AI regulation and sandboxes are still needed. The only binding rule relevant to AI is the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, including profiling, in the Data Protection Act 2021, which is still awaiting a commencement order. In July 2026 the government announced that it intends to develop a national AI policy.
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed again on 18 October 2026 using the Ministry of E-Governance site, the Government Press Office and the Attorney General's Ministry law portal; the National Digital Agenda 2026-2030 was added. The National Assembly's website is still suspended, so pending bills remain unchecked, and the planned national AI policy is tracked as a lead.

instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Belize (House of Representatives and Senate); assented by the Governor-General
instruments.current_status: Enacted as Act No. 45 of 2021 (assent 29 November 2021, gazetted 30 November 2021). Section 97 provides that the Act comes into force on a day appointed by the Minister by Order in the Gazette (different days may be set for different provisions). No commencement order for the Act appeared in the Attorney General's Ministry statutory-instrument listings for 2021-2026 checked on 2026-10-12, so the Act is treated as enacted but not yet in force; the Data Protection Commissioner office it creates has no official sign of being established.
instruments.summary: Belize's general data protection law regulating the collection, keeping, use and dissemination of personal data by data controllers, with GDPR-style principles, data-subject rights and a Data Protection Commissioner as supervisory authority. Section 19 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contract, authorising enactments with safeguards, or consent, and requires controllers to inform data subjects of the existence of automated decision-making. Commencement depends on a ministerial order under section 97.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Belize law with an explicit rule on automated decision-making and profiling (s.19); would govern personal-data processing in AI training and use once in force.

instruments.official_title: National Digital Agenda 2026-2030: Towards a Digital Belize
instruments.english_title: National Digital Agenda 2026-2030: Towards a Digital Belize
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of E-Governance, Government of Belize (endorsed by Cabinet)
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by Cabinet at its meeting of 19 May 2026 as the primary policy framework for all government digital initiatives (Cabinet Brief of 21 May 2026). It covers 2026-2030 and follows the National Digital Agenda 2022-2025. The document itself prints no publication date. It does not create an AI policy; the separate national AI policy announced in July 2026 has not been published.
instruments.summary: Belize's national digital transformation roadmap for 2026-2030, prepared by the Ministry of E-Governance, built on four enablers (governance and coordination, legal and regulatory frameworks, digital talent, digital infrastructure) and a set of pillars and projects. On AI it notes that Belize lacks comprehensive frameworks and dedicated laws, standards and guidelines for AI, and adopts a guiding principle that AI and other emerging technologies be adopted in a targeted and ethical manner that safeguards human rights, equity, privacy and transparency. Its project 'Establish an Artificial Intelligence Strategy', led by the Ministry of E-Governance, plans a national AI Taskforce, ethical and secure AI adoption frameworks and a comprehensive national AI strategy; a tax modernisation project led by the Belize Tax Service plans AI tools for fraud detection, taxpayer profiling, predictive modelling and automated case selection.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Cabinet-endorsed national policy framework that sets the government's expectation of ethical, rights-respecting AI adoption and identifies the need for AI regulation and sandboxes; the only national policy text addressing AI governance in Belize so far.
